issues.description: Indentation bug: version guard for math.exp2 is outside the Math_unary class body, breaking the contract registration
issues.detail: In numba/core/typing/mathdecl.py, the original code had a blank line inside the Math_unary class before the next decorator. The patch removed that blank line and placed `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11): Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` at module scope, but visually adjacent to the class. This works only because `Math_unary` is also module-scoped, but the placement is misleading and fragile. More importantly, the abstract data type here (Math_unary as the ConcreteTemplate contract for unary float operations) is being re-bound under the same name — every subsequent reference to `Math_unary` in the module now refers to whatever `infer_global` returns, not the original class. If `infer_global` ever returns a wrapper rather than the class itself, downstream `infer_global(math.X)(Math_unary)` registrations could silently break. The contract should be: register additional globals against the existing class without rebinding the name.

issues.description: SPEC-MISSING: PYVERSION gating is inconsistent across the three modified modules
issues.detail: The abstract contract being asserted is: `math.exp2` is available on Python >= 3.11 and should be a unary float intrinsic. But the three sites that must agree (typing/mathdecl.py, cpython/mathimpl.py, np/math/mathimpl.py) use two different mechanisms to express the same precondition: mathdecl.py uses `sys.version_info >= (3, 11)`, the two impl files also use `sys.version_info` (requiring a new `import sys` that I don't see added in the diff for cpython/mathimpl.py and np/math/mathimpl.py), and the test uses `PYVERSION` from `numba.core.utils`. The project already exposes `PYVERSION` as the canonical way to express this precondition (the test imports it). All four sites should use the same predicate, and the impl files need `import sys` if they continue using `sys.version_info`. Otherwise this will NameError at import on 3.11+.

issues.description: Missing `import sys` in numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py
issues.detail: The diff adds `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` to both numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py but the diff does not show an `import sys` being added to either file. If `sys` is not already imported at module top, both files will fail with NameError at import time on Python 3.11+. The contract of the module (its import-time precondition) must include every name it uses. Verify whether `sys` is already imported in each file; if not, add it. Better: use `PYVERSION` from `numba.core.utils` for consistency with the test and the rest of the codebase.

issues.description: Release note file is missing a trailing newline
issues.detail: docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst ends with `\ No newline at end of file`. Minor hygiene issue but reST tooling and POSIX conventions both prefer a trailing newline. Add one.

issues.description: Test coverage does not exercise the LSP-relevant contract of math.exp2 (special values)
issues.detail: The contract of `math.exp2` includes specified behavior at boundary values: `exp2(0) == 1`, `exp2(-inf) == 0`, `exp2(inf) == inf`, `exp2(nan) == nan`, and overflow behavior on large inputs. The new test only checks integer and small float inputs ([-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]). Other `test_exp` style tests in this file likely have similar gaps, so this matches local convention, but the substitution contract — that njit'd exp2 behaves the same as CPython's math.exp2 — would be strengthened by adding 0.0, +/-inf, and nan to x_values for the float types. Also note the x_values list contains `-2` twice; likely a copy-paste from `test_exp` but worth cleaning up.

issues.description: Duplicate registration pattern not extracted; ADT seam invites future drift
issues.detail: The same conditional registration appears in three files (mathdecl.py, cpython/mathimpl.py, np/math/mathimpl.py). Each repeats the precondition `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` and the LLVM intrinsic name `'llvm.exp2'`. This is a small ADT-design smell: the contract for 'a unary math function added in Python 3.11 that maps to an LLVM intrinsic' is now smeared across three sites with three near-identical guards. For one function this is fine; for the next four 3.11+ math additions it becomes a maintenance liability. Worth noting for future contributors but not blocking.

review.summary: ADT-SOUND in concept — `math.exp2` is a clean unary float function with a well-defined contract that maps naturally to `llvm.exp2`, and registering it on the existing `Math_unary` ConcreteTemplate is the right modular decomposition. However, the contract's *preconditions* (Python >= 3.11) are expressed three different ways across four sites (`sys.version_info` in three files, `PYVERSION` in the test), and two of those sites likely lack the `import sys` they now require — that's a SPEC-MISSING and a likely import-time NameError on 3.11+. The Math_unary rebinding via `infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` works but is fragile; the indentation also makes it ambiguous whether the registration is intended inside or outside the class body. Recommend: unify on `PYVERSION` everywhere, verify `import sys` is not needed (or add it), tighten the contract test with 0/inf/nan, and add the missing trailing newline to the release note. Decision: needs revision before merge — small but real correctness risk.
